main, steps 1 to 3: memory, timer, folder of the executable
Step 4: load, validate and publish the pack
Steps 5 to 7: single-instance and second-window checks, main returns 0
Gate: FalloutNV links by whole members; in a model at c3ad69b43 one composed statement leaves 34,718 names undefined
S1 crash-log set-up, skipped: waits on the SettingT stand-in and a MessageHandler
S2 to S5 and S7 log and save paths, skipped: wait on catalogue strings and the members that hold their code

nodes.label: vegas-setup prepares vegas-data.pack, catalogue version 2
nodes.source: docs/setup.md (What setup does; Private run on an actual input, catalogue version 2); setup.prepare_pack passes in Windows CI run 43466130320
nodes.detail: vegas-setup reads the player's FalloutNV.exe, identifies the supported original release, reads C1's four strings and the main window class from stored data sections, writes the pack and validates it with the engine's validator. The private run of 2026-11-13 used tool version d5d1d60ec. src/setup and src/main.cpp have not changed between d5d1d60ec and the snapshot commit. include/fnv has changed in twelve headers: seven symbol headers, two per-address declaration headers, the shared NiObject header and the two headers of the shared setting class. VEGAS-13 stays open for the rest of the catalogue.

nodes.label: S2 to S5, the four log paths
nodes.source: docs/data-pack-startup.md (Skipped statements; The user folder buffer); docs/data-pack-catalogue.md (D)
nodes.detail: The four builders are FUN_00c3bb90, fnv_00c3bbe0::FUN_00c3bbe0, FUN_00c3bc30 and fnv_00c3bc80::FUN_00c3bc80. They wait on a later catalogue entry for their four suffix strings and on the members that hold the builders and their buffers. VEGAS-109 repaired the user folder buffer DAT_01202fa0 that the builders copy, and VEGAS-112 repaired DAT_01202b48, S3's destination, which is now an array of 260 characters (491cf9664; objects.path_buffer_extents). Since a76d79f3b FUN_00c3bb80 in tesfile.cpp returns DAT_01202c50, the buffer of S2, as char *. A scratch composition of S2 to S5 into main, linked as FalloutNV links at 11d59dc97, loaded 2,011 members and left 34,719 names undefined. At function granularity it needs blk_00c20000_od.cpp, blk_004c0000_od.cpp, tesfile.cpp and crt.cpp, and three names of the common controls library that blk_004c0000_od.cpp refers to: ImageList_Destroy, ImageList_LoadImageA and InitCommonControlsEx.

nodes.detail: S6 writes the processor count into the setting g_011c3ea4 through FUN_0043d4d0. docs/data-pack-startup.md lists what it waits on: a native owner of that setting, which generated data defines and whose unit's one startup initializer builds it and reads original data (D2); for a native setting, the constructor of INISettingCollection and Setting::IsPrefSetting, which no object defines; a native DAT_01202800, which generated data defines too; and the closure of magicitem.cpp, which defines the accessor. The forced link loses MainStub::FUN_00870bd0. In the section-level reachability model rooted at WinMain, without projection, the body becomes reachable, and through it the model reaches 122 names that no archive member defines; VEGAS-97 counted them on 3503a01a1, and the measurement at c3ad69b43 finds the same 122 among the names that enter that model. This is a count of what a model can reach. It is not a link result, not a run and not a claim about a boot, and all 122 were already undefined in the forced link. The receiver stays open. VEGAS-97 stays in progress for the rest of its census.

nodes.source: docs/boot-real-classes.md (census at 1b3b79d69)
nodes.detail: Their constructor and destructor names are undefined. Binding one needs one declaration of the class that main.cpp and the row's unit share, so that the size that new passes and the fields that the body writes agree. Eight of the twelve are Gamebryo classes. VEGAS-11 owns shared declarations in general.

nodes.label: Shared NiObject with its virtual slot table
nodes.source: docs/shared-gamebryo-bases.md (NiObject; Integration checks; Not covered); include/fnv/ni_object.h, since 0b408d396; docs/boot-real-classes.md (What would let them move); VEGAS-30 ruling (3) of 2026-11-13: bases go base first; VEGAS-11 rulings of 2026-11-13
nodes.detail: Since 0b408d396 include/fnv/ni_object.h declares NiObject on the shared NiRefObject, with no fields of its own, its constructor, its virtual destructor and the 33 virtual functions of slots 2 to 34. Every one of the 33 is open: no function row under the class's name fills a slot, so the names are the spelling of the two units on the header and nothing may be concluded from them. Two units use it. The other copies stay, among them the 62 units on include/NiObject.h, which declares two slots, because their slots or size differ, or, for nicamera.cpp, its NiRefObject is not the shared one. NiObject::NiObject, its destructor and GetType are still undefined. The first unit on the header that emits the class's table binds that table and is not a declaration move. The step changed no object and took no name from the link.

nodes.label: Shared NiObjectNET with its virtual slot table
nodes.source: docs/shared-gamebryo-bases.md (NiObjectNET: decided, the header waits for its first unit); docs/boot-real-classes.md; include/NiObjectNET.h
nodes.detail: The census counts 94 copies, 9 x64 layouts and 2 undecided offsets, and both offsets come from one copy in staging/blk_00a40000_o2.cpp. docs/shared-gamebryo-bases.md decides the declaration: five established fields, the controller being the raw NiTimeController* that the owner counts by hand. It writes no header, because no unit can move today: the only 48-byte copy whose NiObject is shared declares the controller as a NiPointer, six units have a NiObject or NiRefObject copy of their own, and the other copies see another table or have another size. Four rows use a stale 32-bit layout, 0x00a5c200, 0x00a5ba40, 0x00a5b990 and 0x00a5bf50, and are repaired by body under VEGAS-16 before they are respelled.

nodes.label: Constructors that store a table address by hand
nodes.source: docs/boot-real-classes.md (What would let them move); VEGAS-110; VEGAS-110 comment of 2026-11-13
nodes.detail: They are 0x00c46970, 0x00bc2980 and 0x0049ec80, and the member constructor 0x00872ea0. Making them polymorphic changes each constructor's object, so it is a repair with its own object proof, not a declaration move. A VEGAS-110 comment of 2026-11-13 records that three of the four constructors wait on the shared Gamebryo base declarations, because their classes derive from those bases. docs/boot-real-classes.md names the base of 0x00bc2980 only, its NiNode, so the two curated edges name NiNode and NiProperty, which between them need all five bases.

nodes.source: docs/winmain-boot-names.md (WinMain's other undefined names); docs/shared-setting-t.md
nodes.detail: The shared template declares SettingT::Bool, and its row's unit defines it. main.cpp calls 0x00408d60 through stand-ins that return bool* or unsigned char*, where the template's Bool returns SETTING_VALUE*. docs/shared-setting-t.md says the names leave when the unit moves onto the shared template, with an object proof. nodes.source: docs/winmain-boot-names.md (What the steps do not prove); VEGAS-30 ruling of 2026-11-13
nodes.detail: WinMain allocates 0xa4 bytes and FUN_0086c160 builds the object. The compiler measures RenderSystem at 0xB0 bytes on windows-x64, and the bound body touches bytes 0xA0 to 0xB0. main.cpp reads the global through many private classes. FUN_008706b0 passes a 1-byte shell as RenderMgr, which is 0x98 bytes, and as RenderCoordinator, which is 0x8c bytes. No source records an owner or a route for the true size and class.

nodes.detail: Before any program loads misc/main.cpp.obj, no name its link keeps may be in the differing-definitions list. The 0x00870bd0 repair changes one more, a base class descriptor of FUN_00483370, to a copy with other content. These links are models that no program uses.

This is a model result, not a run and not a claim about what a boot reaches, and it was not measured again at the snapshot commit. docs/data-pack-startup.md records a scratch composition of S2 to S5 at 11d59dc97 that loaded 2,011 members and left 34,719 names undefined. The owner has not decided whether to change the link rule.

coverage: The map covers the accepted steps of main in src/main.cpp, in order, and the setup steps that make the pack.
It covers the eight statements of WinMain that main skips, as docs/data-pack-startup.md tables them.
It covers the four boot bodies that WinMain reaches by name, and the contracts that docs/winmain-boot-names.md and docs/boot-real-classes.md record for them, by class and not name by name.
Tickets appear only where a node names them; ticket states are the tracker's on the date above.
limitations: The map is not a call graph. It shows four calls of WinMain and no others; the boot closure has about 21,000 names.

Forced-link counts measure the whole archive. They say nothing about what a running game reaches. VEGAS-30's first criterion is about FalloutNV.exe's own link. Nobody measured which of these names a boot to the main menu reaches.
Estimates are single-name model counts. They are not additive and no link measured them.

The state of a node with a tracker state comes from the tracker's state on the ticket-state date, and curated edges come from tickets, tracker comments and rulings. No machine check confirms them, and they can be stale the day after the snapshot.
